# change-set

> Type-safe change sets for TypeScript. Subclass `ChangeSet`, mark fields with `@attr()`, and
> every assignment is tracked: `dirty`, `changes` and `reset()` on the instance, `value`,
> `dirty`, `mixed` and `reset()` on each attribute. `ChangeSet.fromArray(records)` marks the
> attributes the records disagree on as `mixed`, for editing several records at once.

change-set is experimental and not published to npm. It is one file, `change-set.ts`; copy it
into a project compiled with `experimentalDecorators: true` (it uses TypeScript's legacy
decorators).

## Usage

```ts
import {attr, ChangeSet} from './change-set';

class User extends ChangeSet {
    @attr() name: string;
    @attr() age: number;
}

const user = new User({name: 'Joe', age: 25});
user.name = 'John';
user.attributeFor('name').dirty; // true
user.changes;                    // {name: 'John'}
user.reset();
user.name;                       // 'Joe'
```

## Limits

- The constructor's hash is not type checked; the property setters are.
- A falsy value in the constructor hash (`0`, `''`, `false`) starts the attribute at `undefined`.
- `@hasOne()` and `@hasMany()` are placeholders: the property reads `undefined` and assigning
  to it throws.
